text:
maya: quick design question — playing with the prompt-sets eval runner. thought: allow per-test weights in the scorecard so some tests count more for regressions. sam: ooh yes. where would that live? per-prompt metadata or at the run level? maya: prob both. default = 1 on each test, and an inline weight control when you expand a test row. small numeric stepper, and a compact display in the diff row like "w×1.5". li: is there a concern about clutter? i worry the diff list gets noisy. maybe an "advanced" toggle to show weights. noah: ops/watchers want approval to stay simple — if weights move the needle on pass/fail we need to show computed score and the threshold very clearly. maya: agreed. ui proposal: scorecard header shows "effective score: 82 (threshold 75)" with a breakdown dropdown. hover shows per-test contributions. mock uploaded: figma.com/file/abc123 ara: accessibility nit — our color-only coding for small weight deltas fails contrast. add patterns or a textual delta. also ensure colorblind-safe palette. maya: good call. propose adding +/- icons and a small numeric delta text next to the bar, and an ARIA label that reads "weight changed from 1 to 2". li: keyboard nav question: can the inline stepper be focusable and respond to arrow keys? yes we should. but global single-key shortcuts (eg "a" for approve) are risky when the focus isn't in the runner. sam: +1 for keyboard affordances, but prefer context-aware shortcuts: e.g., when focus is inside the run panel, "k" = jump to next test, "K" = previous. ui-bot: assets uploaded to Figma: figma.com/file/abc123 and screenshots in /designs/eval-weighting-2026.png :pushpin: maya: another feature request — ability to mute a test (exclude it from score) from the overflow menu. tiny confirmation modal required; copy must be explicit that muted tests remain in history but won't affect scores. noah: modal copy suggestion: "Mute this test? Muted tests will be excluded from score calculations but remain in the run history. You can unmute later." :exclamation: ara: also ensure there is an aria-live announcement when a test is muted/unmuted so screen readers pick up the change. example snippet: ```
Test "currency-format" muted
``` li: small copy nit on the approve CTA — current options: "Approve run" vs "Approve changes". which is clearer to non-product folks? sam: i prefer "Approve run" since approval applies to the entire run result. keeps it less ambiguous. maya: another UX problem: compact regression diff mode collapses a lot of context when many tests are collapsed. suggestion: add an "expand all" button and keyboard shortcut (shift+E) to expand/collapse all tests. show a one-line summary per test when collapsed. noah: +1 on expand all. also include an affordance to reveal the last failing output snippet inline so engineers can triage faster. sam: can we ship weights + mute + keyboard as an experiment behind a feature flag and measure engagement? track events: weight_edit, mute_toggle, expand_all, approve_click. maya: yes. acceptance criteria I'll add: - stepper for per-test weight (default 1) with arrow key support - "mute test" action in overflow, confirmation modal copy above - effective score shown with breakdown and threshold highlight - contrast/patterns for diff bars + ARIA labels + live announcements - expand all / collapse all button + keyboard shortcut when run panel focused - telemetry events for weight_edit, mute_toggle, expand_all, approve_click maya: tagging @sam for product, @li for eng implementation, @ara for a11y review. li: i'll pick up tickets for keyboard + focus/stepper behavior. ara: i'll produce an a11y checklist (contrast ratios, aria-live text, focus order) and drop it in the figma file. sam: thanks all — this helps a lot. will prioritize in the next sprint sprint planning. :thumbsup:
